messages:
emma: Heads up — onboarding the new 13B q4f16 build exposed an annoying edge-case with tool/function-call sentinels and role tokens.
raj: repro? what broke exactly?
mike: short tl;dr pls.
emma: tl;dr: HF model used a single special token for `<|tool_call|>` and our tokenizer mapping after quant + vocab merge splits it, which corrupts JSON-mode boundaries and downstream parsing.
sophie: oh no. any crash or just quality regressions?
emma: both. The assistant emits malformed tool payloads sometimes (missing quotes / truncated braces). Also our unit evals show small-but-actionable drop on tool-call suites. eval-bot: regression detected — tool-call-interop suite down 4.8% pass rate vs baseline.
raj: can you paste a minimal example that fails?
emma: here's a reduced prompt (sanitized):
```
<|system|>You are a helpful assistant.<|/system|>
<|user|>Find docs about tokenizers.<|/user|>
<|assistant|>
<|tool_call|>{"name":"search","args":{"q":"tokenizer special tokens","limit":3}}<|/tool_call|>
```
When tokenized with HF tokenizer it yields a single token for `<|tool_call|>` but our quantized tokenizer returns `['<', '|', 'tool_call', '|', '>']` (4 tokens) which splits the JSON payload boundary because we apply JSON-mode start/end detection by scanning for the sentinel token.
raj: ouch. Is this just a q4f16 vocab merge problem or something earlier in preprocessing?
mike: we've seen similar with role tags (`<|user|>`, `<|assistant|>`) when we remapped EOS/CLS tokens during merge. Might be related to how sentencepiece merges punctuation.
sophie: options: 1) add explicit escape characters before the sentinel in prompts (gross), 2) reserve a private-use control token in the vocab and always insert that around tool payloads, 3) change detection to pattern-match angle-bracketed spans rather than token equality. Thoughts?
emma: quick experiments: 1) escape chars — works but brittle and requires prompting changes everywhere. 2) private-use token (we tried U+E000 wrapper) — solved boundary detection but broke some cache key hashing and increased sequence length accounting. 3) pattern-match on raw text — works but we rely on token-level streaming decisions in the runtime, so regressing to raw-text scan kills our streaming decoder heuristics.
raj: can you share the private-use approach snippet?
emma: sure: we prepended `\uE000` and appended `\uE001` around tool payloads at prompt build time. Example: `...<|tool_call|>\uE000{"name":"search"}...\uE001<|/tool_call|>`
sophie: why different start/end codepoints? to avoid collision if one side is missing?
emma: yes, unique pair minimizes accidental collisions. But then we had to teach the tokenizer merge step to map those PUA codepoints to single reserved ids — that's extra work for private deployments.
mike: another idea: use JSON-mode sentinel tokens that are ASCII-sequence but unlikely to be split, e.g., `<<json-begin>>` / `<<json-end>>`. Do we have evidence HF models treat these as single tokens?
emma: inconsistent. HF tokenizer sometimes keeps `<<json-begin>>` as a few tokens depending on BPE/granularity. The only truly consistent approach is reserving a special token id in the target vocab.
raj: for Redwood Private we can ask ops to bake a reserved token at deployment time. But hosted customers / model catalog need automation.
sophie: we should also think about function schema mapping. HF function metadata uses `name`, `description`, `parameters` (JSON schema). Redwood tool tags expect `tool_name` attribute and a top-level `tool_args` JSON blob. Mapping layer currently serializes HF functions into `tool_call` payloads; that mapping assumes sentinel tokens are preserved. If they split, downstream router rejects the tool call.
mike: yeah and quantization experiments increase the chance of splitting because merging algorithms recompute merges and sometimes split long ASCII markers into subpieces.
emma: experiment log (short):
- baseline HF tokenizer: tool-call success 99.7%
- q4f16 naive merged vocab: 86.2%
- q4f16 + PUA wrapper: 99.0% but +0.6 tokens per call on avg
- q4f16 + runtime pattern match on token seq: 97.8% and streaming penalty ~+8ms/token

raj: tradeoffs. For now, what's lowest-friction patch we can ship to hosted?
sophie: propose two-track: (A) implement soft-fallback: if token-level sentinel not found when streaming, run a lightweight raw-text scanner to find `{"name":` inside the last N chars and reconstruct tool payload (still streamable but slower). (B) schedule reserved-token bake for new catalog models; note for legacy models we might not be able to re-tokenize.
mike: +1 for soft-fallback. Also add delta-logging around every reconstructed tool-call so we can see prevalence.
emma: already prototyped soft-fallback. Small patch diff:
```diff
- if (!found_token_sentinel) return fail;
+ if (!found_token_sentinel) {
+   if (raw_scan_for_json_tail(buffer)) {
+     reconstruct_and_emit_toolcall();
+   } else {
+     return fail;
+   }
+ }
```
raj: add unit tests for edgecases: truncated leading `<` or missing `|` or extra spaces injected by tokenizer. Also test role token collisions: e.g., case where `<|assistant|>` is split and merges with `\n` tokens, causing turn boundary mis-detection.
sophie: note: we also saw JSON-mode collisions with function-tagging where the model emitted both inline natural language and a tool payload without a separator. Example: `search: {"name":"x"}` (no sentinel). We need heuristics to detect raw object starts that are intended as tool calls vs plain text. That's fuzzy.
mike: maybe require strict validation: tool payload must be valid JSON and include `name` string matching registered tool names; else treat as content. Add a confidence score.
emma: agreed. Also adding eval harness tests: fuzz with tokenizer splits and synthetic insertions. I propose we run a small canary on hosted traffic before enabling full rewrite.
raj: timeline?
sophie: patch for soft-fallback + logging by EOD tomorrow, canary next week, reserved-token bake tracked as infra ticket (may take 2-3 sprints for marketplace models).
mike: I'll add unit tests and update the onboarding docs with the recommended sentinel requirements (and note quantization caveats).
emma: thanks — I'll upload the repro script and a small charset map to the thread.
eval-bot: new artifact uploaded: tools-token-repro-1765419876.tar.gz — regression trace + corpus.
raj: great. @emma please drop the repro link when ready and tag me. :thumbsup:
